verdicts.title: A Generalized Resolution Proof Schema and the Pigeonhole Principle
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The schematic CERES method is a method of cut elimination for proof schemata, that is a sequence of proofs with a recursive construction. Proof schemata can be thought of as a way to circumvent the addition of an induction rule to the LK-calculus. In this work, we formalize a schematic version of the Infinitary Pigeonhole Principle (IPP), in the LKS-calculus, and analyse the extracted clause set schema. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns schematic CERES cut-elimination and a generalized resolution proof schema for the Infinitary Pigeonhole Principle, extracting a 'Herbrand System' symbolically — it does not measure Herbrand-disjunction length nor tree-resolution leaf counts for finite PHP_n^{n+1}, so it neither supports nor refutes the quantitative log-ratio claim.

verdicts.title: $P \ne NP$, propositional proof complexity, and resolution lower bounds for the weak pigeonhole principle
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Recent results established exponential lower bounds for the length of any Resolution proof for the weak pigeonhole principle. More formally, it was proved that any Resolution proof for the weak pigeonhole principle, with $n$ holes and any number of pigeons, is of length $Ω(2^{n^ε})$, (for a constant $ε= 1/3$).
